text.p: Swedish debt yields ended higher on Thursday, first following higher German and U.S. yields but then tailing negative domestic factors such as a weaker crown.
The nine year bond yield rose six basis points to 7.33 percent. The six month T-bill rate fell two basis points to 4.54 percent.
Dealers said the market was still affected by a Swedish government report published earlier this week that recommended Sweden not join the EMU at the start in 1999.
"The government's EMU commission report is still affecting the market negatively," one analyst said.
The crown weakened against the mark to 4.3760 compared to 4.3570 Wednesday late afternoon, in part due to a weaker dollar.
The central bank said there could be further room to lower its key interest rate, the repo rate, and noted stronger signs of economic recovery during the autumn.
The Finance Ministry said Sweden will cease net borrowing in foreign currrency next year.
The Riksbank ended its board meeting without announcing any changes to its key interest rates.
None of these factors had any market impact, dealers said.
